title: Looplicator DAW 3: feed the loop, fuel the machine
summary: From the legacy PHP engine to a Rust-powered browser DAW: seven mixers, a new React interface, animated playback, and faster ways to turn loops into more loops.
body:
Looplicator is built around a simple idea: make loops out of loops. Feed it a few samples, let a mixer pull them apart and recombine them, then keep the results that make you want to hit play again.

The 3.x release brings the Rust engine and a new React interface together in one project. This first release note covers the jump from the previous 1.13 Vue frontend to 3.0, plus the workflow improvements arriving in 3.1.

A loop machine in your browser

The engine began in the legacy PHP tool. Its Rust port runs as WebAssembly in the browser, and the new interface puts processing in a background worker. Mixer calculations can finish without blocking the controls. Jobs can be cancelled, and processing has a timeout.

Your samples stay in your browser library. Audio processing does not require uploading them to an application server. Browser storage belongs to the browser and origin you use, so keep downloads of loops you want to preserve.

Seven mixers, including dim

The current mixer lineup is mosaic, delayer, xfade, outbreaker, m4ze, samplicat, and dim. Dim is the newest port: slowed, low-pass-filtered material with a delayed channel and an optional modulated second layer. It is a way to push familiar loops into darker textures.

The port follows the legacy effect ordering, but uses a different resampler. Expect the same approach rather than bit-identical output from the PHP/SoX tool. Mosaic construction also avoids repeatedly rewriting its growing output, reducing unnecessary processing.

Less player chrome, more waveform

The React interface replaces the browser's default audio controls with compact transports. Generated loops autoplay, and an animated playhead shows their position directly on the waveform. Click or drag to seek, or focus the waveform and use the arrow keys. Playback includes pause, stop, looping, and mute.

Library previews are compact too. Icon buttons keep the workspace focused on the samples, mixer, FX, tempo, and output.

Choose your kind of random

Mixer and FX each have a shuffle button. Turn one on to choose the eligible options with checkboxes. After generation, the dropdowns show the mixer and effect that were actually picked. You can also apply a new random effect to the current output.

Keep the good ones quickly

Download a WAV, save a loop to the library, or star it as a favorite beside the output. Saving and starring the same output updates its library entry instead of creating duplicates.

  • F generates a new loop.
  • S saves the current loop.
  • X saves it as a favorite.

Shortcuts stay out of the way while you are editing controls. Tempo controls include locking and a random BPM range; tempo adjustment changes speed and pitch rather than detecting the source BPM or preserving pitch.

Try it

Add at least three WAV samples, choose a mixer and optional FX, then press F. Listen, experiment, and keep what works. Current inputs are limited to 60 seconds and 40 MB per sample.

A growing machine, with a record of its changes

More of the legacy tool remains to be ported, alongside new features and experiments. This news section will document those changes as they arrive. Every deployment also keeps a versioned app archive, so earlier releases remain accessible.

Visit the previous Vue release, v1.13.0, revisit v3.0.0, or open the v3.1.0 archive.
